content:
Learn about Pelham Services, the freight transportation team connecting California and Florida through dedicated transport, consolidation and transloading.

Home/About

Pelham Services is run by people who treat freight like it's their own — from dispatch to delivery.

Built around one lane, done right.

Pelham Services started with a simple observation: shippers moving freight between California and Florida were stuck choosing between big national carriers with no personal accountability, and small operators without the network to back it up.

We built Pelham to be the alternative — an integrated fleet-and-warehouse operation with terminals in Gardena, CA and Miami, FL, transloading facilities across five cities, and a team that answers the phone when something needs to change.

Safety, punctuality, transparency

Safety

Every load, every terminal and every driver operates under the same standard — no shortcuts, no exceptions.

Punctuality

We build schedules we can actually hit, then we hit them — because your customers are waiting on ours.

Transparency

Clear pricing, honest timelines, and a straight answer when something goes wrong — not after we're asked twice.

title: Freight logistics trends and what they mean for shippers
content:
Explore freight logistics trends, visibility and route planning, with practical questions for shippers moving cargo between California and Florida.

Home / News / The Future of Logistics

News

September 28, 2025 · By Pelham Services

Logistics doesn't stand still. New technology, new regulation, and rising client expectations show up every year, and the carriers that stay ahead are the ones actively adjusting rather than waiting to be forced into it. At Pelham Services, we treat that as part of the job — here's where we see the industry heading, and what it means for how we run our own network.

Greener, more deliberate routing

Shippers are asking harder questions about the environmental footprint of their freight, and that pressure is only going to grow. For a carrier running a fixed coast-to-coast lane like ours between California and Florida, the most immediate lever isn't a wholesale fleet overhaul — it's cutting the waste that's already baked into the network. That means tighter route planning to reduce empty miles, and using our transloading facilities in Los Angeles, Jacksonville, Tampa, Orlando and Miami to shift freight between trailers and containers at the right point in the journey instead of hauling it further than necessary. We're also keeping an eye on alternative fuel options as they mature, without committing to anything before it's proven at scale.

Real-time visibility as the baseline, not the upgrade

Clients used to accept a phone call as an update. Now they expect to see where a load actually is, get a realistic ETA, and hear about an exception the moment it happens rather than after the fact. That shift in expectation is permanent, and we're building toward it — treating live tracking and proactive communication as a standard part of the service rather than something we charge extra for or reserve for our biggest accounts.

Last-mile pressure keeps climbing

E-commerce growth keeps raising the bar on final-mile speed and reliability, and that pressure doesn't stay contained to parcel carriers — it flows upstream into how quickly freight needs to move through consolidation points and out to its final destination. Our approach is to lean on freight consolidation: combining shipments from multiple shippers so loads move with better density and fewer wasted trips, which keeps the final leg faster without cutting corners on how the freight is handled.

Where this leaves us

None of these trends are about chasing novelty. They're about tightening the parts of the network we already control — routing, transloading, consolidation — so that when the industry moves, we're not scrambling to catch up. That's the posture we're taking into the next few years: watch closely, adopt deliberately, and keep the coast-to-coast lane running the way our clients expect it to.

Tell us what you're shipping between California and Florida, and we'll get back to you with a straight answer.

Home / News / How Pelham Elevates Logistics in CA & FL

Company

September 27, 2025 · By Pelham Services

Reliability and agility aren't optional in today's supply chain — shippers need to know a load will move on schedule, and that if something changes mid-route, someone with real authority over the truck and the warehouse can actually fix it. That's the problem Pelham Services was built to solve on the California–Florida lane.

An integrated fleet-and-warehouse model

A lot of logistics providers outsource pieces of their network — the trucking to one contractor, the warehousing to another, the final mile to a third. Every handoff between those parties is a place where a shipment can get delayed, mishandled, or lost in a communication gap. Pelham takes a different approach: we own and operate both the transportation assets and the storage/transloading facilities ourselves. Fewer handoffs means tighter control over scheduling, handling, and risk from pickup to delivery.

Pool distribution across high-density corridors

In busy corridors across California and Florida, we consolidate goods from multiple shippers into the same trailer, which improves load factors, cuts down on empty miles, and lowers per-unit cost for everyone sharing the lane. It's the same logic behind our freight consolidation service — smarter loading, not just more trucks.

Local presence, coast-to-coast reach

Our strongholds are Los Angeles, Gardena, and Miami, with additional transloading capacity in Jacksonville, Tampa, and Orlando. That combination gives us a genuine local presence at both ends of the country's busiest coast-to-coast freight lane, backed by the terminal network described on our locations page.

Safety and compliance

Pelham operates as a registered motor carrier. Specific FMCSA safety-rating figures, inspection history, and carrier-authority details are Contact our team for current information. — we'd rather leave this section incomplete than publish a safety claim we haven't independently verified with current records. This will be updated with sourced figures once confirmed.

Why it matters to shippers

None of this is abstract — it's the difference between a carrier that can tell you exactly where your freight is and why, and one that has to call three different subcontractors to find out. If you're evaluating a logistics partner for the California–Florida lane, that's the question worth asking any provider, including us.

title: Planning around US freight logistics challenges
content:
Understand US freight logistics challenges, from capacity and fuel costs to planning freight shipments between California and Florida.

Home / News / Navigating Challenges in U.S. Logistics

News

September 28, 2025 · By Pelham Services

Running freight in the United States right now means operating on thin margins while absorbing shocks that are largely out of any one carrier's control — fuel prices that move week to week, a driver pool that hasn't kept pace with freight volume, regulatory requirements that shift, and customers who expect more transparency than the industry has traditionally offered. None of that is unique to us. What matters is how a carrier is built to absorb it.

Fuel price volatility

Diesel prices swing, and a lot of carriers pass that swing along to customers as a vague line-item that's hard to question. Our answer isn't to pretend the volatility doesn't exist — it's to be plain about how and when surcharges move, so the number a client sees on an invoice is one they were already told to expect. If you want a current rate on a specific lane, the fastest way to get a straight answer is to request a quote directly rather than work off a stale published rate card.

Driver and capacity shortages

The industry-wide driver shortage has pushed a lot of freight onto the spot market, where capacity and pricing can change overnight. We manage around that by running our own fleet rather than depending purely on brokered capacity. Owning the trucks and the drivers on our core California–Florida lane means we're not left scrambling for space when the broader market tightens — the capacity we've committed to a client is capacity we actually control.

Regulatory and compliance shifts

Rules around hours of service, emissions, and cross-border documentation don't stay still, and a loose network of independent owner-operators can be slow to adjust when they do. Because we operate as a directly-operated carrier with our own terminals in Gardena, CA and Miami, FL, compliance changes get implemented across one operation instead of negotiated across a patchwork of subcontractors. That's a structural advantage, not a marketing line — it's simply easier to move fast on a rule change when you're not waiting on someone else's fleet to catch up.

What this adds up to

None of these pressures are going away, and we're not claiming to be immune to them. What we can offer is a carrier that's built with fewer moving parts outside our own control — our own trucks, our own terminals, and pricing practices that don't hide the ball. That's what stability looks like in a market this unpredictable.

title: Dedicated freight transport between California and Florida
content:
A full truckload. A focused plan.

Dedicated freight transportation gives a shipper capacity planned around a particular lane or recurring need. It is a different conversation from booking space for every individual load: your origin, destination, frequency and equipment needs shape the plan.

A practical option when your freight fills a trailer, your volumes recur, or keeping one shipment on one load matters. If your freight does not fill a truck, compare freight consolidation and LTL shipping before choosing a service.

How to plan your freight shipment

01

Define the lane

Share pickup and delivery locations, recurring frequency and requested dates.

02

Describe the freight

Explain dimensions, weight, packaging and any handling or equipment needs.

03

Confirm the plan

Review capacity, timing and operating requirements with the Pelham team before booking.

What to include in your freight quote

Your origin and destination, requested dates, cargo description, dimensions and weight give the team a useful starting point. Add equipment and handling requirements rather than assuming they are included.

Request a freight quote

Read the freight quote checklist or contact Pelham Services to discuss the details.

Questions before you ship

What is dedicated freight transportation?

Dedicated transport plans truck capacity around one shipper’s freight or recurring lane, rather than combining that load with other shipments.

How does dedicated trucking differ from LTL shipping?

Full truckload transportation uses one trailer for one shipper’s load. LTL freight shares trailer space. Consolidation brings compatible smaller shipments together; the right choice depends on your load and requirements.

What do I need for a dedicated trucking quote?

Send origin and destination, requested dates, load dimensions and weight, packaging, equipment needs and recurring frequency if applicable. Availability and transit expectations are confirmed during the enquiry.

title: Freight consolidation between California and Florida
content:
Smaller shipments. One considered load.

Consolidated freight shipping combines compatible shipments moving in a similar direction. Instead of reserving a full trailer for a smaller load, shippers can explore a shared transport plan. Compatibility, handling and timing need to be reviewed together.

Worth discussing when your shipment is less than a full truckload, your schedule has room for a shared plan, and your cargo can be handled alongside compatible freight. For a full trailer or a shipment that must stay separate, compare dedicated freight transportation.

How to plan your freight shipment

01

Describe your shipment

Provide pallet or piece count, dimensions, total weight and packaging.

02

Review compatibility

Discuss cargo, destination, handling needs and requested dates with the team.

03

Confirm the shared plan

Review the proposed consolidation arrangement, service conditions and quote before booking.

What to include in your freight quote

Your origin and destination, requested dates, cargo description, dimensions and weight give the team a useful starting point. Add equipment and handling requirements rather than assuming they are included.

Request a freight quote

Questions before you ship

What are freight consolidation services?

Freight consolidation groups compatible smaller shipments into a shared load. It is a planning approach for using trailer space more efficiently, not a guarantee of a fixed saving or transit time.

What is the difference between LTL and FTL?

LTL means less-than-truckload: your freight uses part of a trailer. FTL means full truckload: a trailer is assigned to one shipper’s load. A consolidation enquiry helps determine whether a shared arrangement fits your freight.

What information helps you evaluate consolidated freight?

Cargo description, dimensions, weight, pallet count, packaging, pickup and delivery locations, requested dates and special handling needs. The team will confirm compatibility and available service.

title: Transloading services for the next leg of your freight
content:
New equipment. The same freight journey.

Container transloading services move freight between equipment types: for example, from an inbound container to a domestic trailer. The important decision is how the transfer supports the next leg of your shipment, including packaging, cargo handling and the outbound plan.

Useful when your equipment changes between origin and destination, a container load needs an outbound trailer, or freight needs to be split or combined before the next leg. For a load that can remain on one trailer, explore direct dedicated transport.

How to plan your transloading transfer

01

Plan the transfer

Share the inbound equipment, cargo details, requested location and outbound destination.

02

Confirm handling

Review packaging, dimensions, weight and any special requirements before the transfer is arranged.

03

Connect the next leg

Coordinate the outbound equipment and freight plan with the team; confirm availability and operating requirements.

What to include in your freight quote

Your origin and destination, requested dates, cargo description, dimensions and weight give the team a useful starting point. Add equipment and handling requirements rather than assuming they are included.

Request a freight quote

Read the freight quote checklist or contact Pelham Services to discuss the details.

Questions before you ship

What is transloading?

Transloading transfers freight from one container or trailer to another piece of equipment for its next transport leg. It differs from a journey that stays on one trailer throughout.

Can I enquire about Los Angeles or Miami transloading?

Yes. Include the requested California or Florida location in your enquiry. You can also include Jacksonville, Tampa or Orlando in your enquiry; the team will confirm the appropriate location and available handling for your load.

What should I provide for container transloading?

Inbound equipment type, cargo description, dimensions, weight, packaging, arrival details if known, and outbound destination. Ask the team which documentation and appointment information your particular transfer requires.

title: Transloading vs. cross-docking: how to choose
content:
Start with the equipment change

Transloading describes moving freight from one piece of transport equipment to another. An inbound container might need an outbound trailer for the next part of a journey. Cross-docking describes a flow through a handling point with little or no storage between inbound and outbound movements. The terms overlap in some operations, but they do not describe the same decision.

Ask what your load actually needs

First establish the cargo, inbound equipment, outbound destination and packaging. Ask whether the goods stay together, need to be split, or must be combined with other freight. Handling, inspection and timing should be discussed before a transfer is arranged. A label such as cross-docking cannot tell you which steps your particular shipment requires.

Confirm the service rather than assuming it

Pelham offers transloading enquiries. Cross-docking is discussed here as a general logistics concept, not as a confirmed additional Pelham service. Ask the team about your load, requested location and next transport leg. Do not assume storage, customs clearance or a direct rail or port connection is part of a transfer.

title: LTL vs. FTL for California–Florida shipments
content:
Two ways to use a trailer

LTL means less-than-truckload: a shipment takes part of a trailer. FTL means full truckload: a trailer is assigned to one shipper’s load. The comparison starts with the space and weight of your freight, but handling, timing and the need to keep a shipment separate matter too. A full trailer is not automatically the best option for every shipment.

When shared space is worth discussing

For a smaller load, freight consolidation brings compatible shipments together on a shared plan. Provide pallet or piece count, dimensions, weight, packaging and any special handling needs. Compatibility and available arrangements need confirmation. Do not decide based only on a universal pallet threshold: equipment and the freight itself affect the space available.

When to discuss a dedicated load

Dedicated freight transport is worth discussing when your load fills a trailer, recurring volume needs a planned lane, or keeping freight together is important. Share origin, destination, frequency and requested dates. The team should confirm capacity and service conditions rather than treating a category name as a transit or equipment guarantee.

Explore freight consolidation services and dedicated freight transportation. Send the same shipment details for your freight shipping quote, so the discussion is grounded in one clear set of requirements.

title: What to include in a freight quote request
content:
Give the route and requested dates

Start with pickup and delivery locations. Include the city, state and postal code, plus a street address when it is known. Explain requested pickup and delivery dates, appointment constraints and recurring frequency if applicable. Distinguish a preferred date from a fixed requirement so the team can ask the right follow-up questions.

Describe the load precisely

Provide a cargo description, pallet or piece count, dimensions, total weight and packaging. Note whether freight can be stacked and whether handling or equipment needs require discussion. An overall pallet count without dimensions or weight leaves important parts of the transport plan unanswered.

Identify the service question

Tell the team whether you are exploring dedicated transport, freight consolidation or transloading. If you are unsure, describe the shipment instead of forcing it into a category. For a transfer, add inbound equipment and the intended outbound destination.

Use the form, then confirm the details

The Pelham freight quote form asks for your name, email, origin, destination and message. Company, phone, service and equipment fields add useful context. Submission is an enquiry, not a booking confirmation. Ask the team to confirm the proposed service, operating requirements and quote before arranging freight.

title: How a freight fuel surcharge works
content:
What the surcharge represents

A freight fuel surcharge is a pricing component that addresses fuel cost variation. How it is calculated depends on the agreed carrier or service terms. Some arrangements reference an index or a schedule; others use a different basis. The existence of a surcharge does not establish its percentage, effective date or calculation method.

Ask for the basis and effective date

Request the current basis, calculation method and effective period for your actual quote. Ask whether the amount is already included in the quoted total or listed separately. A historic fuel price, an example from another carrier or an undated webpage is not a reliable substitute for the terms of the service you are considering.

Compare quotes consistently

Use the same lane, freight details and requested dates when comparing quotes. Check which charges are included and which operating conditions could change the total. Avoid comparing a base transport figure from one quote with an all-in figure from another. Ask the team to clarify any line item you cannot explain.

Get the current Pelham information

Contact Pelham Services or request a freight quote for the current terms on your shipment. This guide explains the concept; it does not publish a Pelham surcharge rate, formula or numerical example without confirmed operational data.

Explain whether the shipment remains together or needs to be separated. Those details help identify the questions to resolve before the next leg is planned.

Organize the information you already have

Keep available shipment references, cargo details and arrival information together. A packing list or other shipment document may help explain the load, but the required documentation depends on the actual arrangement. Ask the team which references, approvals or appointment information are needed; this guide is not a universal paperwork checklist.

Confirm handling and equipment

Discuss how the freight is packaged, what equipment changes, and any handling constraints. Ask about acceptance and availability for the requested location. Do not assume storage, hazardous-material handling, customs services, rail access or port access is included. Confirm those points explicitly if they are relevant to your load.

Plan the outbound leg as well

A transfer needs a next transport plan, not only an arrival point. Explore transloading services, compare dedicated freight transport or consolidation when appropriate, and send your details through the freight quote form.

Plan your next freight move

Share your shipment, lane and timing with the team. Confirm the service and operating requirements before booking.
